history.en: Sircar identifies Trisrota only with the Tista river. Bengali tradition places the Bhramari Devi shrine at Salbari near Jalpesh in the Jalpaiguri district, while some accounts place it at Bodaganj near the Baikunthapur forest. The map pin marks Salbari, near Jalpesh, and is approximate. The nearby Jalpesh temple, on the Jarda river 7 to 8 km from Maynaguri, worships Shiva as Jalpesh; it was founded in 1524 by Bishwa Singha, father of the Koch king Nara Narayan, and rebuilt in 1563 and 1663.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's left foot fell here.

en: The pitha takes its name from the Tista, called Trisrota, 'the river of three streams'.
Its exact site is uncertain; local traditions differ between Salbari and Bodaganj.
The Jalpesh temple nearby was badly cracked by the earthquake of 26 April 2015.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.

nearestRail.en: New Jalpaiguri is the main railway junction of the region.
